# R7: Clean-clone reproducibility check

<img src="../assets/statsbomb_logo.png" alt="Hudl StatsBomb logo" width="220">

*Generated by `python -m recruit.run_r7` from `results/r7_clean_clone_check.json`, which
`python -m recruit.clean_clone` wrote from the check's own logs and comparison. Do not edit the numbers
by hand.*

## What this check does, in plain words

A portfolio project is only convincing if someone else can rebuild it. This check starts from an empty
folder outside the repository: it clones the repository, installs the pinned packages into a fresh
virtual environment, points `data/raw/` at the existing StatsBomb and transfermarkt-datasets download
(nothing is downloaded again), runs every step from R1 to R6 in order, and then compares every file the
steps produced in `results/`, `docs/` and `README.md` with the committed copy, one by one.

What may differ, and why (`config/reproducibility.yaml`):

- **Run-time fields** in JSON files (dropped at any depth before comparing): These fields describe the computer run (time, memory, database file size), not the football or the market; they are expected to differ on every run. The DuckDB file size depends on when DuckDB checkpoints and on which later milestones' tables the file held when R1 measured it (the committed R1 figure was carried over from the first full run, PROGRESS.md R6). A JSON file counts as matching if it is identical once these keys are dropped at any depth. Every ignored path is listed in the record.
- **R2 floats:** DuckDB sums floats in parallel, so the order of additions varies between runs and R2's per-90 distributions differ at the 15th-16th significant digit (about 1e-15 relative, NOTES.md R6). A relative tolerance of 1e-9 is a million times wider than that noise and far below any digit the docs print (two decimals). Only R2 gets a tolerance; every other file must match exactly.
- **Markdown lines:** Markdown files (README.md, docs/) print run-time fields (times in s, memory and the DuckDB size in MB). A changed line counts as a run-time line only if it carries one of these units AND is identical to the committed line once every number is masked, so wording or structure can never change unseen. A results figure printed on such a line cannot slip through either: every number in the docs comes from results/*.json (tests/test_readme.py, tests/test_report_r5.py), and those files are compared exactly apart from run_time_keys. The changed lines are saved in the record for review.

### Tests that failed in the clone

| Failed test | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_publication.py::test_nothing_from_data_or_event_level_would_be_committed` | Caused by the check itself, and it found a real gap. The clone's data/raw is a symlink to the download, and .gitignore said "data/raw/": a trailing slash matches directories only, so git listed the symlink as an untracked file that could be committed, and the commit-safety test flagged it. Nothing from the data was at risk (a symlink holds only a path). Fixed in R7 by writing "data/raw" and "data/processed" without the slash; with that .gitignore copied into the clone the test passes (4 of 4 in tests/test_publication.py, re-run by hand after the check). The fix is not committed yet. |

## Time and memory (8 GB MacBook)

The whole check took 4.40 minutes, of which 0.30 minutes were the
package install. The six steps took 237.80 seconds in all. Peak memory of any step:
1,387 MB resident (run_r2), 2,297 MB macOS peak footprint.

| Step | Seconds | Max resident memory (MB) | macOS peak footprint (MB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| run_r1 | 205.57 | 1,127 | 1,907 |
| run_r2 | 13.38 | 1,387 | 2,297 |
| run_r3 | 5.68 | 186 | 155 |
| run_r4 | 4.16 | 277 | 218 |
| run_r5 | 8.52 | 247 | 213 |
| run_r6 | 0.46 | 68 | 52 |

Time and memory are measured by `/usr/bin/time -l` around each whole step. R1's time covers the
fingerprint check of all raw files, the flatten, the load and the audit (R1's own record times only the
flatten step).

## What was run

1. `git clone --branch main` of the local repository into a temporary folder; the committed
   `results/`, `docs/` and `README.md` were copied aside as the reference before any step ran.
2. A fresh venv: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .`, `pip check`.
3. `data/raw/` symlinked to the existing download (no re-download).
4. `run_r1` (full), `run_r2`, `run_r3`, `run_r4`, `run_r5`, `run_r6`, each under `/usr/bin/time -l`.
5. `pytest` and `pytest -m realdata` in the clone.
6. `recruit.compare_runs` on `results/`, `docs/` and `README.md`, and sha256 of every parquet file
   under `data/processed/` against the working copy.

This note and `results/r7_clean_clone_check.json` record the check, so they are not part of it. The
check ran on the committed R6 code: R7's own changes (dashboard polish, this check's code) were not
committed yet, so they were not in the clone.
